# S61 — Split parts: lead and parts in one worktree

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-10-28** — Spec filled 2026-10-28 with owner decisions (opt-in per run, parallel when disjoint max 3, one cap slot).

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

A split lets a large slice use a lead and parts with disjoint files, so parts can change different files at once. ork runs one implementer today and has no split run. The slicer contract puts the parts in the slice worktree (../slicer/src/slicer/ai.py:400), so this slice must not give each part its own worktree.

From S10 (carried here from S08): split-part and sliver prompts need the same 'no handoff before review' wording as the implementer prompt.

## Implement

Owner decisions 2026-10-28 (interactive): a split run is opt-in per run (`ork run ID --split` and a toggle in the launch confirm; never automatic); parts run at the same time only when their files are disjoint, at most 3 at once (matrix rule u7), otherwise one after another; a split run counts as one run against the project and global caps. Tests first; re-anchor line numbers from the code. 1. Roles: add lead and part to internal/roles/roles.go with prompts lead.md and part.md (both carry the 'no handoff before review' wording from S10; a part changes only its own files and runs no slicer write command, ai.py:334-336). 2. Plan: with --split the daemon asks RecommendRoles with split yes for the parts' rows and no for the lead's; the plan shows lead and part rows and the owner confirms as for any plan; a plan that changed since the confirm is refused (S161 rule). 3. Engine: the lead round returns a parts list (part id, files, tests); ork checks the files against the slice's Files section and for overlap, groups disjoint parts into batches of at most 3, runs each batch's parts in the one slice worktree, then runs one review and one gate on the combined diff; the architect only on size L (record 123). A part that fails its own check or touches a file outside its list fails the round and goes back to that part once. 4. Ledger and record: each part is a step with --parent on the lead's step; the run record keeps parts so the TUI run tree shows them (internal/tui/runtree.go). 5. Docs: design.md:184-193, glossary.md:31-35 and 151, dashboard.md run tree. UI slice: UI pass (r14).
